title: HyCaMi: High-Level Synthesis for Cache Side-Channel Mitigation
problem: Cache side-channel attacks compromise cryptographic implementations, particularly block ciphers; existing automatic hardening methods using Boolean circuits achieve security but suffer from significant performance overhead.
motivation: Cache side-channels pose a major threat to cryptographic implementations and are widely exploited to break security guarantees in practice.
method: HyCaMi automatically converts block cipher implementations (encryption algorithms that process fixed blocks of data) into hardware designs using Lookup Tables—memory arrays storing pre-calculated values. Because table lookups always follow the same memory access pattern regardless of input data, they prevent cache side-channel attacks (where attackers infer encryption secrets by observing which memory locations get accessed). HyCaMi then uses quantitative analysis (mathematical measurement) to determine how much security leakage remains and lets you adjust table sizes to balance speed and security.
key_novelty: The core idea is quantifying cache leakage to automatically balance security and performance through adjustable lookup tables in block cipher hardening.
contributions: LUT-based automatic hardening method for block ciphers against cache side-channels
9.5× efficiency improvement over prior Boolean circuit-based approaches
Quantitative static analysis framework for verifying security guarantees
Tunable speed-security trade-off mechanism through variable LUT sizing

metrics.other: cache side-channel leakage reduction with tunable security-performance trade-off

limitations: Trade-off mode reduces maximum leakage guarantees to achieve faster performance; scalability to larger ciphers and broader cryptographic primitives not discussed.
primary_theme: Automatic cache side-channel protection for block ciphers via LUT-based synthesis
